D2 — When the webhook job retries, do receivers get duplicates, and how do we prove the chosen behavior?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-ORkyrO on main, plan "Add background job retry framework".
ELI10: Today a webhook is sent at most once: if it fails, it fails, but the receiver never gets the same event twice. Turning on retries means a webhook that was actually delivered but whose job crashed right after can be sent again. Receivers that bill, email or create records on each webhook will double up. We have to choose on purpose: keep "never twice", or retry and give receivers a key so they can spot the repeat. Whatever we pick needs a test that fails if someone breaks it later.
Stakes if we pick wrong: duplicate webhooks cause double charges or double notifications downstream, or, if we keep no-retry, transient failures silently drop deliveries, which is today's behavior but now unexpected next to retried workers.
Recommendation: B because the plan's purpose is to retry failed work, and an idempotency key is the standard, cheap way to keep duplicates harmless; pick A only if receivers cannot dedupe.
Completeness: A=8/10, B=9/10, C=4/10

A) Keep at-most-once (no retry) (human: ~2 h / CC: ~10 min)
  ✅ Zero risk of duplicate side effects at receivers; nothing changes for consumers
  ✅ One small regression test proves the guarantee and guards the rewrite
  ❌ Webhook deliveries still die on the first transient failure, the exact pain the plan exists to fix
B) At-least-once + idempotency key (recommended) (human: ~1 day / CC: ~30 min)
  ✅ Failed webhooks are actually redelivered, and receivers can discard repeats by key
  ✅ Three focused tests pin the contract: retry happens, key is stable across attempts, no re-send after success
  ❌ A consumer-facing contract change: receivers must honor the key, so it needs documentation and possibly a consumer heads-up

  ✅ Smallest change; retries work immediately with no header or doc work

D3 — How many times does a failing job retry, and what happens when it gives up?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-ORkyrO on main, plan "Add background job retry framework".
ELI10: A retry curve says how long to wait between tries, but not when to stop. A job with a bug in it, or a payload the code can never handle, will fail every time. Without a limit it retries forever and quietly eats worker capacity. When it does stop, we need to keep the job's data and the last error somewhere a human can look at it and re-run it after a fix; otherwise the failure vanishes.
Stakes if we pick wrong: poisoned jobs loop forever and starve healthy ones, or exhausted jobs are dropped with no payload and no error to debug, so the user's work is silently lost.
Recommendation: A because a cap plus a replayable dead-letter record is how every mainstream job library already behaves, and the record is what makes a 3am failure diagnosable.
Completeness: A=9/10, B=6/10, C=2/10
Pros / cons:
A) Cap 5 + dead-letter record (recommended) (human: ~half day / CC: ~15 min)
  ✅ Poisoned jobs stop after a bounded number of tries and stop stealing capacity from healthy ones
  ✅ Exhausted jobs keep payload, attempt count and last error, so an engineer can diagnose and replay after a fix
  ❌ Someone has to own the dead-letter set; without an owner it becomes a graveyard (alerting is a separate choice)
B) Cap 5, library default failed state (human: ~1 h / CC: ~5 min)
  ✅ Bounded retries with almost no extra code; relies on whatever the library stores by default
  ✅ Fewer moving parts than a custom dead-letter record
  ❌ If the library's default failed state lacks the last error or attempt count, exhausted jobs are hard to diagnose or replay
C) Unbounded retries (plan as written) (human: 0 / CC: 0)
  ✅ No job is ever declared failed; transient outages of any length eventually recover
  ✅ Nothing to configure or test for exhaustion
  ❌ A job that can never succeed retries forever, consumes worker slots and hides the bug indefinitely
Net: trading a small amount of exhaustion handling and ownership for bounded worker load and diagnosable, replayable failures.

options.label: Cap 5 + dead-letter record (recommended)
options.description: Configure a per-worker max-attempts value through the library hook (default 5). D3 — How many times does a failing job retry, and what happens when it gives up?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-ORkyrO on main, plan "Add background job retry framework".
ELI10: A retry curve says how long to wait between tries, but not when to stop. A job with a bug in it, or a payload the code can never handle, will fail every time. Without a limit it retries forever and quietly eats worker capacity. When it does stop, we need to keep the job's data and the last error somewhere a human can look at it and re-run it after a fix; otherwise the failure vanishes.
Stakes if we pick wrong: poisoned jobs loop forever and starve healthy ones, or exhausted jobs are dropped with no payload and no error to debug, so the user's work is silently lost.
Recommendation: A because a cap plus a replayable dead-letter record is how every mainstream job library already behaves, and the record is what makes a 3am failure diagnosable.
Completeness: A=9/10, B=6/10, C=2/10
Pros / cons:
A) Cap 5 + dead-letter record (recommended) (human: ~half day / CC: ~15 min)
  ✅ Poisoned jobs stop after a bounded number of tries and stop stealing capacity from healthy ones
  ✅ Exhausted jobs keep payload, attempt count and last error, so an engineer can diagnose and replay after a fix
  ❌ Someone has to own the dead-letter set; without an owner it becomes a graveyard (alerting is a separate choice)
B) Cap 5, library default failed state (human: ~1 h / CC: ~5 min)
  ✅ Bounded retries with almost no extra code; relies on whatever the library stores by default
  ✅ Fewer moving parts than a custom dead-letter record
  ❌ If the library's default failed state lacks the last error or attempt count, exhausted jobs are hard to diagnose or replay
C) Unbounded retries (plan as written) (human: 0 / CC: 0)
  ✅ No job is ever declared failed; transient outages of any length eventually recover
  ✅ Nothing to configure or test for exhaustion
  ❌ A job that can never succeed retries forever, consumes worker slots and hides the bug indefinitely
Net: trading a small amount of exhaustion handling and ownership for bounded worker load and diagnosable, replayable failures.
Header: Retry cap
Options:
A) Cap 5 + dead-letter record (recommended)
Configure a per-worker max-attempts value through the library hook (default 5). On exhaustion the job moves to the library's failed/dead-letter set keeping payload, job id, attempt count, last error and stack, so it can be replayed. Required proof: attempt below cap re-dispatches; attempt at cap lands in the failed set with attempts and last error recorded. Human: ~half day / CC: ~15 min. Completeness 9/10.
